editorial:
Imagine you are a cool college professor who always supports your students. You believe in their right to protest and change the world. That is exactly where you start in this story. Anthony Quinn plays a man caught in the middle of a campus takeover during the wild days of the late 1960s. When the college president quits because of the chaos, the students pick him to lead. You get to see a really interesting struggle as he tries to keep his liberal values while stopping the school from turning into a total disaster. It feels like a high-stakes debate that never stops, making you wonder if you would be able to keep your friends and your job at the same time.

Quinn is amazing here, bringing a lot of heat and emotion to every scene. The movie moves along well, though some of the talking parts might feel a bit long if you prefer action movies. It is a great pick if you like stories about power and politics. To get the best experience, you should look for it to rent on Apple TV or see if you can find a high-quality version on Prime Video. If you are a movie collector, adding a physical copy to your shelf is a great way to keep this piece of history. It is a solid watch that makes you think about where to draw the line.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with the professor realizing that total freedom without any rules leads to violence. He finally takes a stand against the most radical students to save the school. He stops the anarchy by using his authority to bring back order, even though it means some of his former allies now see him as a traitor. He chooses the safety of the community over the wild goals of the revolution.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and stories about clashing beliefs.
